sections.title: Beyond the framework

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: These ideas come up when interviewers check whether you can shape a codebase, not only add to one.

rows: A model is valid inside a boundary
"Customer" differs in billing and support: often a service boundary
A consistency boundary, changed as a unit
`Order` protects its lines; one transaction per aggregate
`Money` as a record, never a raw `double`

blocks.title: Do not over-apply it
blocks.text: Simple CRUD does not need DDD. Use it where the business rules are the hard part.

sections.title: Layered versus hexagonal

blocks.title: Hexagonal architecture
blocks.code:
flowchart LR A[REST controller] --> B[Input port] C[Kafka listener] --> B B --> D[Domain and use cases
no framework imports] D --> E[Output port] E --> F[JPA adapter] E --> G[HTTP client adapter]
blocks.caption: Dependencies point inward: the domain knows interfaces, and adapters implement them.

blocks: Layered controller-service-repository code is fine for most services. Hexagonal pays off when domain logic is rich, or several inputs and outputs must be swappable and tested without a framework.

sections.title: Decisions, debt and multi-tenancy
blocks: **Architecture decision records (ADRs)** are short files that record the context, the decision, the options rejected and the consequences. They answer "why is it like this?" a year later.
**Technical debt** should be argued in business terms: "this module caused 3 of the last 5 incidents, and changes take twice as long" gets time allocated. "The code is ugly" does not.

rows: One missing filter leaks data; use row-level security

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **Monolith or microservices for a new product?** Usually a well-modularised monolith first. Microservices solve team and scaling problems at the price of distributed-systems problems. Split when a boundary and a real reason exist, such as independent deployment or scaling.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- A bounded context is often the right service boundary.
- One transaction per aggregate; use events between them.
- Use hexagonal only where the domain justifies it.
- Record decisions, and argue debt in business terms.

items.question: Why is one transaction per aggregate a useful rule?
items.answer: It keeps locks small and makes later splitting possible. Other aggregates are updated through events, with eventual consistency.

items.question: How do you convince a manager to fund a refactor?
items.answer: Show its cost in incidents, delivery time or defects, propose a small incremental step, and say how you will measure the improvement.
